newsitem.title: HUNGARY: NATO must not boost Hungary defence budget-Suranyi.
newsitem.headline: NATO must not boost Hungary defence budget-Suranyi.

text.p: Hungary's central bank chairman Gyorgy Suranyi said he hoped the country's accession to NATO would not mean a significant increase in military spending.

"I really do hope that (NATO membership) is not going to create any substantial increase in military expenditure," Suranyi told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview broadcast on Thursday.

The 16 NATO countries invited Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic on Tuesday to start talks intended to lead them to membership in 1999. But they made little mention of equipment compatibility requirements or the cost of NATO membership.

Hungary has said that it is anxious to meet demands by NATO for military compatibility with Western armies and will increase its defence budget from a current 1.8 percent of gross domestic product to 2.2 percent in the years ahead.

But despite plans for an eventual purchase of up to 30 new jet fighters for up to $1 billion, Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti suggested on Thursday that costly arms would take a back seat to military basics such as command and control.
"The economic stability of the Republic of Hungary is an important factor that will have to be taken into account," he said during a visit by U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen.
Suranyi said funds for new equipment would have to be found within the existing defence budget framework.
"I believe (in) very reasonable restructuring of the military expenditure with tightening in other areas of the military budget," he said.
